newsitem.title: FINLAND: INSTANT VIEW - Mixed reaction to Helsinki summit.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Mixed reaction to Helsinki summit.

text.p: Following are comments from economists about the results of the summit.
CHARLES BLITZER, European emerging markets economist at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette in London:
"Very welcome is the emphasis on trade and investment rather than on foreign aid and money transfers."
"This is recognition of progress Russia made as well as recognition of the steps Yeltsin's government is starting to implement in a new round of reforms."
CATHERINE MACDOUGALL, Russia analyst at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson in London:
"The American impact on the Russian economy is minimal. It's up to the Russians to sort out their tax code, their regulatory framework, their oil legislation and their tax revenue."
"It's up to Russians and it's going to be sorted out, hopefully, by the new cabinet and I do think the new cabinet is the good news as far as the market is concerned."
"It wasn't really up to the Americans to approve of or disapprove of WTO or Paris Clus membership."
"The market has become much more micro-sensitive and less sensitive to political news."
"Overall, of course it will mean more investment, but the summit will not be a major facilitator of investment into the Russian economy."
GUNNAR TERSMAN, Russia analyst at Sweden's Handelsbanken in Stockholm:
"The result is not totally unexpected....it's in line with what the U.S. has said before.

"Russian membership in the WTO would mean more liberal trade policies and that Russia would be treated more favourably by other trading partners. But the United States is only saying they have set a target and this does not mean it will happen."
"Yeltsin sitting down with Clinton doesn't mean it will be any easier to get this done. But, if they carry through all these things, it will mean more investment."
